text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST

- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu doesn't rule out tax cut. Treasury will submit proposal for additional budget cut of some two billion shekels to the cabinet in about two weeks. Commentary calls it "budget brinkmanship".
- Treasury bought same property in city of Rehovot twice -- in 1959 and 1988 -- because it has no inventory of state-owned properties, Treasury officials admit.
- Koor Industries Ltd may sell 24.5 pct share of food distributor Tami -- Israel Edible Products -- to U.S.-based CPC International Inc.
- Indigo NV reports $13.8 million in losses.
- Australian firms look to invest here; Sunshine Consolidated Industries and Israel Aircraft Industries consider carbon fibre factory.
- U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk reassures Netanyahu there has been no change in policy on Jewish settlements.
- Prime minister to Assad: Let's return to negotiations.
- Israeli military report details series of Palestinian Authority violations of Oslo peace deal.
- Survey due to be made public later this week alleged to show a majority favour Tel Aviv over Jerusalem as capital.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor: We are at the edge of the abyss; we'll try not to raise the tax burden.
HAARETZ
- Labour Minister Eli Yishai says licences will be cancelled of contractors who illegally import foreign workers.
- Token drop in interest rates next Monday; meaningful reduction will depend on the budget.
- From January to October 1996, CIS immigration to Israel dropped by 8 percent compared with same period in 1995.
- Israeli army requests restraint by its South Lebanon Army militia allies in order to moderate Hizbollah responses to Israel.
- Some 130,000 teachers will receive as their annual gift cellphones valued at 50 million shekels at Treasury expense.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- The plan: Budget cut of 7 billion shekels and after that a lowering of interest rates by two percent.
- Bank of Israel will allow banks to provide services in customers' homes.
- Personnel changes in IDB group: Leon Recanati to be chairman of Clal.
- 70 percent of largest organisations in Israel suffer from computer break-ins.

- Andorra offended by Netanyahu's saying he favours Palestinian self-rule entity like Andorra, something short of state. In letter, prime minister of Andorra writes: "For your information we are an independent state."
MAARIV
- Under consideration: Cancellation of income tax breaks and sacking of thousands of public workers. For first time prime minister and finance minister won't rule out raising tax burden.
- IDB Chairman Rafael Recanati attacks Netanyahu, says he cannot tolerate fact prime minister not a wanted guest in any country in the world.
- Political sources say consideration being given to land for peace formula with Syria.
- Would-be Labour party leader Ehud Barak says the party is dead -- and people are running away from it.
